title: M³OPD-Reasoner Lifts Qwen3.5-9B 6.5% Across 21 Benchmarks
summary: VinUniversity and A*STAR release M³OPD-Reasoner, an open distillation recipe that pushes Qwen3.5-9B from 70.0% to 77.1% across 21 multimodal benchmarks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- VinUniversity and A*STAR released M³OPD-Reasoner, a fully open distillation recipe that boosts Qwen3.5-9B from 70.0% to 77.1% across 21 vision-language benchmarks.
- The method distills three domain-expert teachers (image STEM, image perception, video) into one 9B student, then applies mixed reinforcement learning for a 6.5% overall gain.
- Video reasoning shows the largest improvement at +10.7%, while the team open-sourced 1.35M training samples, 193K RL pairs, and all checkpoints.


Researchers from VinUniversity and A*STAR have released M³OPD-Reasoner, a fully open training recipe that lifts a nine-billion-parameter Qwen3.5 student from 70.0% to 77.1% average accuracy across 21 vision-language benchmarks. The method distills three domain-expert teachers (image STEM, image perception, video) into a single student via Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation, then applies a shared reinforcement-learning pass on top. The team has published the full training corpus, RL dataset, code, and every intermediate checkpoint.


Officially released on November 18, 2026, the recipe arrives in a crowded season for open distillation approaches and marks one of the first public demonstrations of consecutive MOPD and mixed-RL stages applied to a compact multimodal model.


## How the Distillation Pipeline Works


The authors begin by training one Qwen3.5-9B teacher per domain using Group Sequence Policy Optimization. Each teacher specializes in a narrow slice: one handles image-based STEM problems, another tackles general image perception tasks, and a third focuses exclusively on video reasoning. Once the three teachers are ready, the team distills all of them into a single 9B student through Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation, a technique that samples on-policy rollouts from each teacher and aggregates the signals into the student's training.


After MOPD converges, the pipeline adds a mixed reinforcement-learning stage that reuses the same prompt set employed by baseline mixed-training runs. The paper notes that this two-stage structure (MOPD followed by MixRL) has not been studied in prior vision-language model recipes, and the results suggest the stages compound rather than overlap.


## Performance Gains by Domain


Video reasoning absorbs the largest improvement, climbing 10.7 percentage points on average. LongVideoBench jumps 12.3 points, Video-Holmes rises 10.3 points, and other video-centric evals follow similar upward trends. Image STEM tasks gain 5.1 points on average, with EMMA adding 14.5 points and LogicVista contributing 12.0 points. Image perception shows a narrower +3.0% gain, which the authors report without additional commentary.


MOPD alone, before the added MixRL pass, already scores 76.6% across the benchmark suite, clearing the 74.9% mark achieved by mixed-training baselines. The final MixRL stage pushes the student to 77.1%, a 6.5-point gain over the original Qwen3.5-9B baseline of 70.0%.


## Open Data and Checkpoints


VinUniversity and A*STAR have released the M³OPD-SFT-1.35M supervised fine-tuning corpus, the M³OPD-RL-193K verifiable-reward set, the complete training codebase, and every checkpoint produced during the pipeline. The release covers each intermediate teacher, the post-MOPD student, and the final post-MixRL model. Practitioners can reproduce the full training run or adapt individual stages to their own multimodal architectures.


The datasets span image STEM, image perception, and video reasoning prompts, with verifiable reward signals annotated for the RL stage. The paper and all artifacts are hosted on Hugging Face, following the team's stated goal of enabling reproducible research in compact vision-language distillation.


## What This Means


M³OPD-Reasoner demonstrates that domain-expert distillation followed by shared reinforcement learning can extract significant performance from a small multimodal model without scaling parameter count. The 6.5-point overall lift and double-digit gains in video reasoning suggest that specialized teachers, when distilled carefully, transfer complementary skills that a single mixed-training run may dilute. With the full recipe, datasets, and checkpoints now public, teams building compact vision-language systems have a reproducible baseline for multi-teacher distillation and a clear path to testing whether the MOPD-then-MixRL staging generalizes to other model families.
